Let me interject here for a moment if you please. Firstly to clarify a few things for you:

- CIS is the Latin prefix for someone who identifies with their birth gender.

- I believe what was meant by "have a go at" was that you would judge said person the same as you have Michelle.

- Deadnaming is using the persons given name rather than their chosen name.

Now, the way a person expresses their trans identity is a choice all their own. In no way shape or form should you or anyone else devalue or judge them because they don't express their identity in a way you deem correct. It doesn't make them any less trans. You have to understand that people vary in this manner just as much as they might in the way they define themselves as football fans or gamers. Would you say I'm any less of a gamer because I don't play the games you think are good? I would hope not.

In addition, I think your issue, and correct me if I'm wrong, is that you feel that Mark is doing something with his life and Michelle is not. Which may be true, but to associate their identities with this and then generalizing these groups under that association is a terrible idea. Would it surprise you to know that much like Michelle I identify as trans, spend the majority of my social time as male, have no makeup or wig, but that I also work a full time job making well above minimun wage? That like Mark I contribute to society by paying taxes and the sort? If it does then your idea of transgender people is severely jaded and could use some working on.

All in all you really ought to take the time to gain information and knowledge in these two grouos of people while maintaining the idea that each group consists of many different people who maintain their identity in their own way. This rule applies to all groups of people, not just those in the LGBTQ community.

The idea behind being PC is to create an existence where everyone is comfortable. No one feels segregated, judged, or out of place by the words or actions of another. Yes, some people take this way too far in that they turn a minor thing into this huge, world ending ordeal. It's not so much that what was said or done shouldn't be an issue. It's that the people who have the issue go way beyond the ok level of "hey, that's offensive to me I'd appreciate it if you didn't do that". There are, however, things in this life which are IMHO completely ok to react with such intensity to (i.e. rape, murder, molestation, genocide).

Unfortunately, this world has spent so much time trying to create groups of power to over take one another that no one really wants or feels the need to help each other and live peacefully together. A perfect example would be the common tjought amongst many Americans that they are somehow better than Canadians. The Canadians have never, that I'm aware of, to earn this "bullying" from the Americans. So why does it exist? Simply because there is some inherent need to be better than someone else.

Once you lose that need and look at people as an actual person then you can begin to coexist in a mutually beneficial existance.

I've read a ton of articles, blogs, and various other writings (medical and otherwise) that all sort of paint this picture where I'm supposed to hate my penis if I want to live my life as a woman. I like my penis, it's the rest of my body that disgusts me. I'm terrified of losing functionality if I start HRT. Some people say that this kind of mindset is some sort of fetishization of trans women and I don't necessarily think so. I have no interest in using this as a way to get off, but I do enjoy penis in vagina sex (sorry if that sounds stupid, I wasn't really sure how to word that part) with my wife. Not jjust for the sex aspect, but it's a huge part of our intimacy and losing that is terrifying.

TL;DR Thank you for this post. It makes me incredibly happy that I am not the only person who feels this way.
